topologies.name: mesh-30
topologies.description: Mesh gossip topology: N=30 services, K=6 random peers each (seed=424242).

topologies.name: mesh-50
topologies.description: Mesh gossip topology: N=50 services, K=8 random peers each (seed=424242).

topologies.name: scale-50
topologies.description: 50-node layered topology: 1 gateway + 4 mid-tier (svc-a/b/c/d) + 45 leaf nodes. Designed for gossip protocol evaluation at scale (N≥20).

profile.name: adaptive-surge
profile.description: Naprzemienne bursts + degradacja — profil nieznany parametrom static

profile.name: baseline-flaky
profile.description: Persistent 40% packet loss on 3 of 5 services (svc-01, svc-03, svc-05) via tc netem throughout the experiment. Models chronic unstable network on majority of ring nodes. With 'none' strategy expected SR ~60-80%; adaptive strategies should recover toward 100%.

profile.name: burst-failure
profile.description: 80% packet loss on 2 services (svc-02, svc-04) from t=15s to t=40s, then recovery. Models a sudden DDoS-like burst affecting specific nodes. Adaptive strategies should circuit-break within seconds; 'none' strategy sustains 80% loss for full 25s burst window.

profile.name: cascade-crash
profile.description: svc-03 receives SIGKILL at t=20s; svc-01 receives SIGKILL at t=35s. Docker restarts each container (restart_policy: on-failure). Models cascading crash scenario: first failure triggers spike in load on remaining nodes, second failure arrives before full recovery. Tests whether adaptive strategies prevent cascade amplification.

profile.name: network-partition
profile.description: L3 network partition injected at the gateway: all traffic between the gateway and {svc-01, svc-03, svc-05} is dropped by iptables (both INPUT and OUTPUT rules) from t=5s to t=75s. Unlike tc netem packet loss (L4, probabilistic), iptables DROP is deterministic (100% loss) and models a split-brain scenario where the gateway cannot reach a subset of backends while other services remain functional. Peer IPs are resolved at runtime via Docker DNS (service name → bridge IP). Overlay designed to be stacked on top of baseline-flaky, exposing superposition of L4 packet loss (affecting the same 3 leaves) and L3 reachability failure. peerServices field is non-standard — consumed by coordinator.js, resolved to IPs before being passed to infrastructure-fault-injector as options.peerIps.

profile.name: no-wan
profile.description: No base-layer WAN latency — intra-bridge traffic keeps sub-millisecond RTT. This is the original configuration used for the published 120-experiment matrix, preserved as a base alongside wan-50ms for cross-comparison.

profile.name: slow-degradation
profile.description: Linear latency increase 0→5000ms over 60s on svc-01 and svc-03 (via tc netem, updated every 1s by InfrastructureFaultInjector). Models progressive WAN congestion. Pre-emptive strategies (backpressure, mas-agent) should detect the upward trend via gossip and reroute BEFORE timeout threshold; reactive strategies wait until errors accumulate.

profile.name: wan-50ms
profile.description: Constant 50ms ±10ms egress delay applied ONLY to the gateway container's eth0 at t=1s, persisting for the entire experiment. Models a WAN hop between the application gateway and a remote data center hosting the leaf services. Leaf-to-leaf traffic (ring gossip) is unaffected, matching the design intent that intra-DC gossip remains fast. Since gateway is the only node issuing outbound routing HTTP calls to leaves, applying WAN to its egress is sufficient — HTTP RTT is dominated by the slower direction. This is a BASE layer intended to be stacked under an active overlay fault (baseline-flaky, burst-failure, slow-degradation, cascade-crash) via the FAULT_BASE coordinator env var, answering reviewer concern about external validity under realistic inter-DC latency.

profile.name: wan-baseline
profile.description: Constant 50ms ±10ms inter-container latency applied to all ring-50 services from t=1s, simulating a DC-to-DC WAN link as a permanent baseline condition. NOT one of the paper's original four fault profiles — this is future-work validation for the external validity concern raised in Section 2 (Threats to Validity). With 50ms RTT and gossip interval 3000ms, ring-50 convergence takes ~2.5s per hop vs ~5ms at zero baseline. Use alongside an active fault profile (e.g. baseline-flaky) to test whether strategy rankings hold under non-zero baseline latency.
